justification: The evidence demonstrates that the AI system maintains high classification accuracy (above 90%) under various stressed and perturbed conditions, including field removal (93.7%), OCR degradation (92.1%), formatting variations (91.6% to 94.8%), and predefined perturbation tests (92.8%, 90.9%, 93.4%). Additionally, it shows a highly robust out-of-distribution mechanism, successfully flagging 1,127 out of 1,200 (93.9%) OOD documents. This systematic evaluation, which has been independently reproduced, strongly supports attributing operational robustness.
evidence_used: With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
An out-of-distribution test set contained 1,200 documents from document classes excluded from training.
Of the 1,200 out-of-distribution samples, 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
The validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
A separate validation team reproduced the reported tests.
limitations: The evidence does not specify the actual operational threshold required for safety or compliance in this specific medical administrative context, though the performance degradation across perturbations is minor.
